name: a live reference is silent and a forgotten one is stale
brief:
## Now
- 🚧 Dispatched the migration (session:1a2b3c4d) — still running.
- ✅ Dispatched the docs pass (session:deadbeef) — landed?

## Recently
- 2026-08-01  something (session:cafebabe)
why: The whole verb in one case: a brief writes SHORT references and the store holds full UUIDs, so matching is by prefix in whichever direction is longer; and only `## Now` is checked — `Recently` is a dated log that is SUPPOSED to name dead sessions, so flagging its entries would make the report unreadable.

findings.detail: session:deadbeef is not a session this host still knows about, so this Now line has outlived its dispatch. If the work landed, move the entry to Recently (or archive it); if it is still yours, re-dispatch and write the new session id. Nothing was changed.

expected.note: 1 of 2 ## Now entries need YOUR judgement (1 name sessions that are gone). This check only reports: it never edits, moves or deletes a line, because the user's own brief edits are authoritative. Act on them with a board move or an explicit edit.

name: a finished session counts as gone, and so does an archived one
brief:
## Now
- Dispatched the port (session:1a2b3c4d) — waiting on it.

findings.text: - Dispatched the port (session:1a2b3c4d) — waiting on it.

why: The question a Now line answers is 'is this dispatch still running', not 'did this session ever exist' — a worker that finished cleanly is PRECISELY the case that leaves the line behind, so a copy that counted it as live would be blind to the checker's main quarry. `liveSessions: 1` is the control: the predicate is not simply refusing everything.

findings.text: - Dispatched the port (session:1a2b3c4d) — waiting on it.

name: a malformed reference is flagged even beside a good one
why: `session:6a-round2` is a real transcription bug from a live manager — a nickname where a session id belongs — and half a broken line is still a broken link in the user's brief, so it is reported even though the entry ALSO names a session that resolves. The entry still counts as live, because it is.

findings.detail: session:6a-round2 is not a session id, so it links to nothing. Fix the reference by hand (or re-append the line with brief_append's sessionId param, which validates it) — this check does not edit the brief.

expected.note: 1 of 1 ## Now entries need YOUR judgement. This check only reports: it never edits, moves or deletes a line, because the user's own brief edits are authoritative. Act on them with a board move or an explicit edit.

name: a dispatch-shaped line with no reference is flagged and ordinary prose is not
brief:
## Now
- Dispatched a worker to fix the flake, no id written down.
- A standing note the user wrote themselves.

findings.text: - Dispatched a worker to fix the flake, no id written down.

why: Precision over recall: a checker that cries wolf is one a manager stops reading, and an ignored checker is worse than none because it still costs a tool call. So a reference-less entry is flagged ONLY when the wording leaves no doubt, and the user's own standing note is left alone.

findings.text: - Dispatched a worker to fix the flake, no id written down.
findings.detail: this reads like a dispatch but names no session:<id>, so nothing can tell you whether its worker is still alive. Add the reference when you next touch the line.

expected.note: 1 of 2 ## Now entries need YOUR judgement. This check only reports: it never edits, moves or deletes a line, because the user's own brief edits are authoritative. Act on them with a board move or an explicit edit.

name: an upper-case reference is normalized and a long one matches by prefix
why: References are canonicalized to the short form (a UUID's first group, lower-cased) before matching, and the prefix comparison runs in whichever direction is longer — so a manager that wrote more of the id than the store holds still resolves, rather than being told its own live worker is gone.

expected.note: Every ## Now entry (1) either names a session this host still knows about or is not a dispatch line. Nothing to prune.
